name: Self-tanning mousse

lead: Self-tanning mousse is a foam applied to the skin that contains dihydroxyacetone (DHA), a sugar-derived compound that darkens the surface of the skin. It is applied with a mitt and develops over hours.
Color lasts about a week as the outer skin sheds, and it is a UV-free alternative to sunbathing for looking tanned.

paras: DHA reacts with amino acids in the outermost dead skin cells in a Maillard-type reaction, forming brown pigments called melanoidins. It does not involve melanin or UV, so it does not activate the skin's own tanning response. Reviews note minimal to no photoprotective value.

Streaks, orange tones and uneven fading are the main nuisances. Reviews of DHA describe a good topical safety record but call for more research on inhalation from sprays and booths, and the color additive is for external use only. The product tans you without UV but does not protect you from sun, and some studies find sunless tanner users still use less sun protection.
